svg.text: A day in the life of a packet, with the code: RX and TX on a ConnectX NIC with the mlx5 driver
Same flow as the overview drawing. Each box adds, in purple, the main functions and structs that do its job (or, for hardware, set it up), so you can find it in the source.
the kernel copies the data into the app's buffer
IP and TCP check the packet, queue the data on the socket, wake the app
unmap, free the skb, wake the queue
build the skb and headers; the qdisc and XPS pick the SQ
each CQE → skb around the filled buffer (no copy), XDP, GRO
same core; TX CQs first, then RX, budget 64
DMA-map the data, write a WQE into the SQ
fresh buffers into the RQ, then re-arm the CQ
MMIO write to the NIC's UAR page
takes the next RQ WQE, writes the packet into that buffer, then a CQE
set up by: en_main.c mlx5e_create_rq → CREATE_RQ
if the CQ is armed: EQE, then MSI-X
reads the WQE, then the packet data, later writes a CQE
set up by: en_main.c mlx5e_create_sq → CREATE_SQ
parse, steering + RSS pick the RQ, check checksums, strip VLAN
calculate checksums, TSO cuts big sends, insert VLAN
asked for by the WQE built in mlx5e_xmit:
holds packets for the pipeline; if full: pause / PFC, or drop
picks which SQ sends next: QoS, rate limits, pause
runs setup commands from the driver:
create rings, steering rules, MTU, link.
RX: find the frame, check the FCS (CRC),
TX: add the preamble and the
MTU: port.c mlx5_set_port_mtu counters: en_stats.c (PPCNT register) → ethtool -S
RX: recover the clock, turn the signal into bits,
TX: encode, add FEC, turn bits
into an electrical or optical signal
speed: port.c mlx5_port_set_eth_ptys FEC: en/port.c mlx5e_set_fec_mode link up/down: en_main.c mlx5e_update_carrier
Port: RJ45 (copper BASE-T) or SFP / QSFP / OSFP cage (DAC / optical)
module info: port.c mlx5_query_module_eeprom (ethtool -m) link settings: en_ethtool.c mlx5e_ethtool_set_link_ksettings
1 channel = 1 core: 1 IRQ, 1 NAPI, 1 RQ + its SQs
read (dashed) = DMA read or CPU read
code that does or sets up the box

File names are relative to drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/ in the Linux kernel (en_rx.c, en_tx.c, en_txrx.c, en_main.c, eq.c, pci_irq.c, cmd.c, ...). Indented lines are called from the line above. Names follow recent upstream kernels (6.x);
older kernels and DOCA-Host (mlnx-ofa_kernel) may differ slightly. WQE = work queue entry. CQE = completion queue entry. EQE = event queue entry. skb = the kernel's packet object.
